illīc

adverb · Wiktionary

there (location)

In this lexicon

  • there

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Aul. 655: quis illīc est?; Vulg. Ps. 103 (104), 25: illīc rēptilia quōrum nōn est numerus

Examples

  • ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē

    there my little Tullia was waiting for me, on her very birthdayCic. Att. 4.1.4

    In the entry for there

  • in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē. ibi ut sint omnia parāta

    we expect to reach Tusculum on the Nones or the day after. See that everything is ready thereCic. Fam. 14.20.1

    In the entry for there

  • Hoc mare magnum et spatiōsum manibus; illīc rēptilia quōrum nōn est numerus

    this great sea, wide on every side: there are creeping things without numberVulg. Ps. 103 (104), 25

    In the entry for there

  • abscēde etiam nunc — etiam nunc — etiam — ohē, istīc astātō.

    Move back a bit more — more — more — whoa, stand there.Plaut. Aul. 55–56

    In the entry for there

  • vōs, meae cārissimae animae, quam saepissimē ad mē scrībite et vōs quid agātis et quid istīc agātur

    my dearest souls, write to me as often as you can, both how you are and what is going on thereCic. Fam. 14.14.2
